title: Priority-Constrained Descent posted to arXiv
body: The group's optimization framework for hierarchical objectives goes public. PCD preserves the descent direction of the primary objective and modifies it only as far as necessary to guarantee progress on the secondary ones, converging to a condition strictly stronger than Pareto stationarity.
source: Varam and AlHajri, under review at TMLR

title: Dara Varam wins the university-wide Graduate Research Excellence Award
body: The Master's Level Graduate Student Research, Scholarly and Creative Work Excellence Award, awarded across the whole university, together with the CEN Graduate Academic Excellence Award and the 2026 CEN Graduate Research Excellence Award at MS level.
source: American University of Sharjah

title: Dara Varam defends the group's second MSc thesis
body: Priority-Constrained Descent: Hierarchical Multi-Objective Optimization for Deep Learning, the optimization framework now at the center of the group's work, defended for the MSc in Machine Learning.
source: Advisor: Dr. Mohamed I. AlHajri

title: Dara Varam begins a PhD at EPFL
body: Straight from the MSc into a doctorate at the Ecole Polytechnique Federale de Lausanne, continuing on optimization for deep learning.
source: Ecole Polytechnique Federale de Lausanne

title: Amana Vision founded out of the drowning-detection project
body: The ORCA senior design project has become a company. Amana Vision is commercializing the on-site drowning-detection gateway, is in validation and pilot studies, and is being built out inside Sheraa, Sharjah's flagship startup platform.
source: Sheraa, Sharjah Entrepreneurship Center

title: Sub-millisecond, microjoule edge inference published in the IEEE Internet of Things Journal
body: Layer-wise mixed-precision quantization for indoor environment identification, with latency and energy measured on commodity microcontroller hardware rather than estimated. The flagship result behind the group's claim that real models fit on real chips.
source: Abushahla, Noshin, AlHajri and Ali, IEEE Internet of Things Journal

title: Writer identification for historical Arabic manuscripts appears in IJDAR
body: Different Strokes for Different Folks, the group's vision work applied to palaeography, identifying the hand behind historical Arabic manuscripts.
source: International Journal on Document Analysis and Recognition

title: Muhammed Noshin defends the group's first MSc thesis
body: An Alternating Projection Framework for Element-Wise Masked Nonlinear Matrix Decomposition, the work that established the group's second research direction, and the first graduate thesis completed here. He has since joined the MIT Senseable City Lab.
source: Advisor: Dr. Mohamed I. AlHajri

title: Classification of indoor environments in time-varying channels
body: Extending RF environment identification to channels that move, the harder and far more realistic case.
source: Noshin, AlHajri, Ali and Altunaiji, IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters 24(9)

title: Class separation dynamics in vision transformers
body: An empirical study of how a transformer pulls classes apart as depth increases, the groundwork for Lujain Khalil's theoretical bounds on the evolution of separation fuzziness.
source: Varam, Khalil, Darwish and AlHajri, IEEE Access

title: A comprehensive survey of neural network quantization for microcontrollers
body: Methods, platforms and applications gathered into one reference for anyone trying to put a real model on a real microcontroller. Posted to arXiv and under review at IEEE Access.
source: Abushahla, Varam, Panopio and AlHajri

title: Cognitive radio spectrum sensing on the edge
body: A quantization-aware deep learning approach to spectrum sensing that runs on constrained hardware. The paper began life as an undergraduate senior design project in this group two years earlier.
source: Abushahla, Varam and AlHajri, IEEE Communications Letters 29(8), 1988 to 1992

title: Shaheen takes 2nd place worldwide at Dell Technologies' Envision the Future
body: Against 259 teams from 14 countries. Shaheen detects a person from the air at 98.2% accuracy on under 2 MB of memory and 0.895 W of power, then radios their photograph and coordinates to rescue teams over a custom long-range protocol.
source: Yousef Irshaid, Malik Hader, Ahmad Alsaleh, Adham Elmosalamy

title: Shaheen wins 1st place in the AUS senior design competition
body: First in the Computer Engineering track, and a patent filed on the detection and geolocation approach. The project also produced the most comprehensive desert search-and-rescue image dataset in the MENA region.
source: Computer Science and Engineering, American University of Sharjah

title: Muhammed Noshin joins the MIT Senseable City Lab
body: As a Research Fellow, after completing the group's first MSc thesis on nonlinear matrix decomposition.
source: Massachusetts Institute of Technology

title: Outage analysis of THz-enabled IRS-assisted space-air-ground networks
body: Performance limits for reconfigurable intelligent surfaces operating at terahertz frequencies across integrated satellite, aerial and ground links.
source: Benaya, AlHajri, Hassan, Ismail and Landolsi, IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society

title: Period estimation work presented at ICASSP 2025
body: A complex coprime frequency-sum based signal representation for period estimation, presented at the field's flagship signal processing conference.
source: Shah, Ali, Altunaiji, Chakka and AlHajri, IEEE ICASSP 2025

title: Properties of Type-2 complex conjugate pair sums
body: Foundational signal-representation theory and its applications, in the APSIPA transactions.
source: Shah, Chakka, Reddy, Srikanth, Ali, Altunaiji, AlHajri, Olcan and Abd-Alhameed

title: Speaking at the AUS AI Symposium
body: On a panel at the university's artificial intelligence symposium, on where machine learning research meets deployment in the region.
source: American University of Sharjah

title: VR tourism for pediatric oncology patients reaches the Dell global top five
body: A top-5 finalist out of 215 teams at Dell Technologies' Envision the Future 2024, for gamified virtual tourism built for children undergoing cancer treatment.
source: Ananya Sudheer, Ashrita Koshy, Saba Hussain, Zain Kamal Raisan

title: HAPS-mounted IRS-assisted communication analyzed at ICCSPA 2024
body: Outage analysis for a multi-user system served by a reconfigurable intelligent surface mounted on a high-altitude platform station.
source: Benaya, Hassan, Ismail, Landolsi and AlHajri

title: The cognitive radio project featured on Sharjah TV
body: An interview on Sharjah TV about the annual engineering senior design competition and the cognitive radio spectrum sensing project that took second place in it.
source: Sharjah TV

title: VR tourism places 3rd in the AUS senior design competition
body: Third in the Computer Engineering track for the virtual tourism and gamification platform built for pediatric oncology patients, which would go on to reach the Dell global top five that September.
source: Computer Science and Engineering, American University of Sharjah

title: Cognitive radio spectrum sensing places 2nd in senior design
body: Second in the Computer Engineering track. The project became a journal paper in IEEE Communications Letters the following year, the trajectory the group aims for with every undergraduate team.
source: Hamza Abushahla, Ghanim Alali, Sultan Mohamed, Muhammad Sadaqat

title: Conference Operations Chair, IEEE WCNC 2024 in Dubai
body: Dr. AlHajri served as Operations Chair for the IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference, one of the IEEE Communications Society's flagship events, held in Dubai.
source: IEEE WCNC 2024, Dubai, United Arab Emirates

title: Invited speaker at Mufakiru Al Emarat
body: Speaking at the Emirates Thinkers program on artificial intelligence, engineering research and the path from a university laboratory to something that works in the field.
source: United Arab Emirates

title: Joining the American University of Sharjah
body: Dr. Mohamed AlHajri joins the Department of Computer Science and Engineering as Assistant Professor and begins building the group.
source: Department of Computer Science and Engineering

title: PhD awarded by MIT
body: A doctorate in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science with a minor in Applied Mathematics, completed in the Claude E. Shannon Communication and Network Group at the Research Laboratory of Electronics. Thesis: Constrained Information Exchange Message Passing Algorithm in Probabilistic Graphical Models.
source: Massachusetts Institute of Technology

title: Nominated for the IEEE International MGA Achievement Award
body: For the IEEE-UAE Distinguished Seminar Series, which drew more than 3,000 registered participants from over 62 countries and was endorsed by IEEE's President and CEO.
source: IEEE Member and Geographic Activities

title: Invited speaker at the Mohamed Bin Zayed Majlis for Future Generations
body: Speaking on the future of artificial intelligence and engineering education in the UAE.
source: United Arab Emirates

title: IEEE UAE Award of the Year
body: Awarded by the world's largest technical professional organization for the advancement of technology.
source: IEEE United Arab Emirates Section
